agree.reason: She pays her cousin $600 a year and likes him, and the page never says why $199 a month, about $2,388 a year, is better than that, so it gives her little reason to book the call.

honest.reason: Nearly every claim matches the brief and the setbacks are stated openly, but 'One of them saved $800' turns a client's report into a plain fact, and 'you won't spend months teaching me' is a promise the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only restated: there's no annual cost, nothing about 9 of 31 clients reporting lower accountant fees, no on-time rate (9 of 12 closes), and no point that no client has ever left because of the service.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative, a once-a-year catch-up from a relative while she handles payroll and sales tax herself, never appears, so the $800 saving and the monthly fee aren't measured against anything she knows.

qualification.reason: The 10th-of-the-month deadline, the three misses last year and the 10-staff payroll cap are specific and checkable, but nothing says what happens if a close is late.

objections.reason: The page answers objections nobody raised, such as the price rise and being a one-person business, and leaves her main one unanswered: 'my cousin already does this for much less.'

fit.reason: It runs about 340 words, is laid out like a sales page and ends with the booking button as asked.
